shared_elements: upright monolithic stone with rounded/tapering outline
engraved or carved schematic design filling the whole face
arched or curved framing line across the upper part
bilaterally symmetrical composition around a vertical axis
horizontal band of repeated curved/scalloped motifs in the lower zone
concentric or curved enclosing outlines following the stone's edge
justification: Both are single upright stones whose whole face carries a symmetrical schematic design organised the same way from top to bottom: a broad arch or curved yoke above, a straight vertical axis and horizontal members in the middle, and a band of repeated arcs or scallops across the lower zone. The decisive difference is technique and volume — A is worked in raised relief on a thick sculpted block with modelled, rounded forms, while B is a thin, uniform incised outline drawing on a flat slab, so the two could not plausibly be the same hand.
